blocks.text: You can connect your Slack organization to Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance to gain continuous visibility and governance for third-party apps installed in the Slack environment, including automation of your vetting and governance processes.
A user with Admin or Owner roles is required to connect 3rd-Party App Governance to Slack workspace.
To connect Slack to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: Click Connect in the upper-right corner of the App Dashboard.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: From the drop-down menu, select Slack.

blocks.text: See image.
The Add Integration window appears.

blocks.item: In the Add Integration window, click Add. You are prompted to sign in if you haven't already done so.

blocks.text: See image.
A consent window appears (all privileges are read-only), and you can see a detailed list of permissions and data.
See image.

You must select the SSPM Scan checkbox on the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console to enable the SSPM scan feature for the tenant. To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

After a connection is achieved, it might take a while to pull and ingest all relevant application data depending on the size of your tenant. During this time, a message displays indicating that the integration is still being processed. After integration is completed, a success message appears, and the tenant details are updated on the Settings page. You then receive an email from Zscaler when the integration is ready for further review.
You can view the list of added tenants along with information such as integration status, enabled features, first connected time, last synced time, etc. on the Settings page.
You might need to reconnect Slack to 3rd-Party App Governance if an error displays (e.g., Grant Expired). To reconnect Slack to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Reconnect icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.
A consent window appears. After consent is granted, the connection is updated.
You can edit a Slack connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To edit a Slack connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Edit icon next to the relevant integration.
In the Edit Integration window, edit the tenant details as required and click Save.

blocks.text: The connection is updated.
You can delete a Slack connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To delete a Slack connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Delete icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.
The connection is deleted.

Although the app is requesting an "Administer a workspace" permission, 3rd-Party App Governance is utilizing a very limited set of APIs granted by this permission, designed only to read audit and activity logs.

table: Basic information of the user connecting to the application
View the name, email domain, and icon for workspaces your Slack app is connected to: team:read
Basic information about the workspace, such as name, domain, email domain, and icon
View people in a workspace: users:read
Basic information of users in your workspace
View email addresses of people in a workspace: users:read.email
Email addresses of users in your workspace
View user groups in a workspace: usergroups:read
List of user groups in your workspace

Collect workspace access logs and applications (integrations) activities such as consent, revoke, and others. This allows you to measure app usage, and detect suspicious app activity, permission anomalies, and others.
